title: Mountain Pose (Tadasana)
content: Tadasana is the base for all standing poses. It improves posture, strengthens the thighs, knees, and ankles, and helps firm the abdomen.
safety_notes: If you have low blood pressure, avoid standing for too long.

title: Child's Pose (Balasana)
content: A resting pose that gently stretches the hips, thighs, and ankles. It helps calm the mind and relieves stress and fatigue.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a knee injury or diarrhea.

title: Downward-Facing Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana)
content: An energizing pose that stretches the shoulders, hamstrings, and calves while strengthening the arms and legs.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have carpal tunnel syndrome or high blood pressure.

title: Warrior I (Virabhadrasana I)
content: Builds focus and stamina. Stretches the chest, lungs, and shoulders while strengthening the legs.
safety_notes: Keep your gaze forward if you have neck issues.

title: Warrior II (Virabhadrasana II)
content: A powerful standing pose that increases endurance and strengthens the legs and ankles.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have recent hip or knee surgery.

title: Tree Pose (Vrksasana)
content: Improves balance and concentration. Strengthens the spine and legs while opening the hips.
safety_notes: Never place your foot directly on the side of the knee joint.

title: Cobra Pose (Bhujangasana)
content: A gentle backbend that opens the chest and strengthens the spine and shoulders.
safety_notes: Avoid during pregnancy or if you have a recent back injury.

title: Cat Pose (Marjaryasana)
content: Provides a gentle massage to the spine and abdominal organs. Often paired with Cow Pose.
safety_notes: If you have a neck injury, keep your head in line with your torso.

title: Cow Pose (Bitilasana)
content: Stretches the front torso and neck. It warms up the spine and improves posture.
safety_notes: Move slowly if you have chronic back pain.

title: Easy Pose (Sukhasana)
content: A classic seated pose for meditation. It strengthens the back and stretches the knees and ankles.
safety_notes: Sit on a folded blanket if your hips are very tight.

title: Bridge Pose (Setu Bandha Sarvangasana)
content: Stretches the chest, neck, and spine. It also helps alleviate stress and mild depression.
safety_notes: Avoid moving your head side-to-side while in the pose to protect the neck.

title: Plank Pose (Phalakasana)
content: Builds core and upper body strength. It tones the abdominal muscles and strengthens the wrists.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have severe carpal tunnel syndrome.

title: Corpse Pose (Savasana)
content: The ultimate relaxation pose. It lowers blood pressure and calms the central nervous system.
safety_notes: If you have lower back pain, place a bolster under your knees.

title: Bound Angle Pose (Baddha Konasana)
content: Often called Butterfly Pose, it stretches the inner thighs, groins, and knees.
safety_notes: If you have knee or groin injuries, use blocks under your thighs for support.

title: Legs-Up-The-Wall Pose (Viparita Karani)
content: A restorative pose that improves circulation and relieves tired legs and feet.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have glaucoma or serious eye conditions.

title: Staff Pose (Dandasana)
content: The seated version of Mountain Pose. It improves posture and strengthens the back muscles.
safety_notes: If your lower back rounds, sit on a blanket to tilt the pelvis forward.

title: Knees-to-Chest Pose (Apanasana)
content: Helps release lower back tension and aids in digestion by massaging the abdominal organs.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a recent hip injury.

title: Sphinx Pose (Salamba Bhujangasana)
content: A very gentle backbend for beginners that strengthens the spine and stimulates the sacral-lumbar arch.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a recent abdominal surgery.

title: Standing Forward Bend (Uttanasana)
content: Stretches the hamstrings and calves while calming the brain and reducing stress.
safety_notes: Keep knees slightly bent if you have lower back issues.

title: Low Lunge (Anjaneyasana)
content: Stretches the hip flexors and groins while strengthening the legs.
safety_notes: Place a blanket under the back knee if you feel discomfort.

title: Reverse Warrior (Viparita Virabhadrasana)
content: A standing pose that stretches the side body and waist while strengthening the legs and core.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have hip, knee, or shoulder injuries.

title: Extended Side Angle (Utthita Parsvakonasana)
content: Strengthens and stretches the legs, hips, and hamstrings while opening the chest and shoulders.
safety_notes: If you have neck problems, look straight ahead instead of up at the arm.

title: Wide-Legged Forward Bend (Prasarita Padottanasana)
content: A calming inversion that stretches the hamstrings and back while improving circulation to the brain.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have lower back problems or a recent hip surgery.

title: Pyramid Pose (Parsvottanasana)
content: Intense stretch for the hamstrings and spine. It improves balance and digestion.
safety_notes: Keep a slight bend in the knees if you have tight hamstrings to avoid strain.

title: Garland Pose (Malasana)
content: A deep squat that opens the hips and stretches the ankles, lower back, and neck.
safety_notes: Place a rolled-up mat under your heels if they don't touch the floor.

title: Puppy Pose (Uttana Shishosana)
content: A cross between Child's Pose and Downward Dog. It stretches the spine and shoulders deeply.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a recent shoulder or knee injury.

title: Happy Baby Pose (Ananda Balasana)
content: Gently opens the inner thighs and groins while calming the brain and relieving stress.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a knee injury or are pregnant.

title: Seated Forward Bend (Paschimottanasana)
content: Stretches the entire back of the body from the heels to the neck. Helps soothe the mind.
safety_notes: Do not force the fold; use a strap around the feet if you cannot reach them.

title: Hero Pose (Virasana)
content: A seated posture that stretches the thighs and knees. It is an excellent pose for meditation.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a serious knee or ankle injury.

title: Gate Pose (Parighasana)
content: Stretches the side of the torso and the hamstrings. It helps stimulate the abdominal organs.
safety_notes: Keep the knee on a blanket if it feels sensitive on the floor.

title: Lizard Pose (Utthan Pristhasana)
content: A deep hip opener that stretches the hamstrings, hip flexors, and groins.
safety_notes: Use blocks under your hands or forearms to reduce intensity.

title: Supine Spinal Twist (Supta Matsyendrasana)
content: A restorative twist that stretches the back muscles and spine while encouraging detoxification.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a recent back or hip injury.

title: Locust Pose (Salabhasana)
content: Strengthens the muscles of the spine, buttocks, and the backs of the arms and legs.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a serious back injury or headache.

title: Big Toe Pose (Padangusthasana)
content: Stretches the hamstrings and calves. It also helps relieve flat feet and menopause symptoms.
safety_notes: Keep knees bent if you feel any strain in the lower back.

title: Half Lord of the Fishes Pose (Ardha Matsyendrasana)
content: A seated twist that energizes the spine and stimulates the liver and kidneys.
safety_notes: Avoid during pregnancy or if you have a spinal disc injury.

title: Reclining Bound Angle Pose (Supta Baddha Konasana)
content: A restorative pose that opens the groins and hips while calming the nervous system.
safety_notes: Use pillows under the knees if the stretch in the inner thighs is too intense.

title: Thread the Needle (Parsva Balasana)
content: Gently stretches the shoulders, arms, upper back, and neck.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a chronic neck or shoulder injury.

title: High Lunge (Ashta Chandrasana)
content: Strengthens the legs and arms while opening the hips and chest.
safety_notes: If balance is difficult, keep the back heel against a wall for support.

title: Chair Pose (Utkatasana)
content: Strengthens the legs, back, and shoulders. It builds heat in the body and tones the core.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have chronic knee pain or low blood pressure.

title: Downward Dog on a Chair
content: A modified version of Downward Dog that is easier on the wrists and shoulders.
safety_notes: Ensure the chair is stable and placed against a wall.

title: Wind-Relieving Pose (Pavanamuktasana)
content: Excellent for digestion and releasing gas. It also stretches the lower back and neck.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a recent abdominal surgery or hernia.

title: Mountain Pose with Arms Overhead (Urdhva Hastasana)
content: Stretches the belly and improves digestion while firming the shoulders and arms.
safety_notes: Do not look up if you have neck pain; look straight ahead.

title: Thunderbolt Pose (Vajrasana)
content: A seated pose that is ideal for digestion. It can be practiced immediately after a meal.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have acute knee or ankle injuries.

title: Scale Pose (Tolasana) - Modified
content: A modified seated balance that begins to build arm and core strength.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have wrist or shoulder pain.

title: Half Forward Fold (Ardha Uttanasana)
content: Stretches the front of the torso and strengthens the back while improving posture.
safety_notes: Keep the spine flat; do not round the back.

title: Side Plank - Modified (Vasisthasana)
content: A modified side balance with one knee on the floor. Builds core and shoulder strength.
safety_notes: Keep the supporting wrist directly under the shoulder.

title: Goddess Pose (Utkata Konasana)
content: A wide-legged squat that strengthens the lower body and opens the hips and chest.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have recent hip or knee injuries.

title: Crescent Lunge (Anjaneyasana Variation)
content: A variation of the low lunge with arms reaching back to open the heart and lungs.
safety_notes: Be careful not to over-arch the lower back.

title: Deer Pose (Yin Yoga)
content: A gentle seated twist and hip opener that is very effective for improving internal and external rotation of the hips.
safety_notes: If you feel sharp pain in the knees, adjust the angle of the legs.

title: Palm Tree Pose (Urdhva Hastasana Variation)
content: A standing stretch on the tiptoes that improves balance and stretches the entire body.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have frequent vertigo or dizziness.

title: Crow Pose (Bakasana)
content: A compact arm balance that builds wrist, arm, and core strength. It helps overcome the fear of falling and improves focus.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have carpal tunnel syndrome or a wrist injury. Place a pillow in front of you for safety.

title: Eagle Pose (Garudasana)
content: A balance pose that requires focus. It stretches the upper back and shoulders while strengthening the thighs and calves.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have recent knee, ankle, or shoulder injuries.

title: Boat Pose (Navasana)
content: A powerful core-strengthening pose that challenges the abdominal muscles and hip flexors while improving balance.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have low blood pressure, asthma, or a recent abdominal injury.

title: Half Moon Pose (Ardha Chandrasana)
content: A standing balance that stretches the groins and hamstrings while strengthening the spine and thighs.
safety_notes: If you have neck issues, don't look upward; look straight ahead or at the floor.

title: Camel Pose (Ustrasana)
content: A deep heart-opening backbend that stretches the entire front of the body and improves spinal flexibility.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have high or low blood pressure, or a serious lower back or neck injury.

title: Side Plank (Vasisthasana)
content: An arm balance that focuses on the obliques and shoulder stability. It tones the arms and strengthens the core.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have serious wrist, elbow, or shoulder injuries.

title: Pigeon Pose (Eka Pada Rajakapotasana)
content: A deep hip opener that targets the psoas and piriformis muscles. Great for releasing emotional stress held in the hips.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have chronic knee injuries or sacroiliac issues.

title: Warrior III (Virabhadrasana III)
content: A challenging balance that strengthens the ankles, legs, and back muscles while improving overall posture.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have high blood pressure or a recent hip injury.

title: Dolphin Pose (Ardha Pincha Mayurasana)
content: Similar to Downward Dog but on the forearms. It strengthens the core and shoulders and prepares the body for inversions.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have shoulder or neck injuries.

title: Revolved Triangle Pose (Parivrtta Trikonasana)
content: A standing twist that improves balance and digestion while stretching the hips and spine.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a back injury or low blood pressure.

title: Cow Face Pose (Gomukhasana)
content: A seated pose that stretches the hips, thighs, and ankles, as well as the shoulders and chest.
safety_notes: If you cannot reach your hands behind your back, use a yoga strap.

title: Upward-Facing Dog (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana)
content: A backbend that strengthens the spine, arms, and wrists while stretching the chest and abdomen.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have carpal tunnel syndrome or a recent back injury.

title: Four-Limbed Staff Pose (Chaturanga Dandasana)
content: A key transitional pose in Vinyasa. It develops incredible arm and core strength.
safety_notes: Ensure shoulders don't drop below the level of the elbows to prevent shoulder strain.

title: Bow Pose (Dhanurasana)
content: The body takes the shape of a bow. It strengthens the back muscles and stimulates the abdominal organs.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have high blood pressure, a hernia, or recent abdominal surgery.

title: Wild Thing (Camatkarasana)
content: A 'heart-opening' pose that stretches the front of the body and builds strength in the shoulders and upper back.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have carpal tunnel or rotator cuff injuries.

title: Extended Hand-to-Big-Toe Pose (Utthita Hasta Padangusthasana)
content: A standing balance that requires strong hamstrings and steady focus.
safety_notes: Use a strap or keep the knee bent if the hamstrings are tight.

title: Fish Pose (Matsyasana)
content: A backbend that opens the chest and throat. It is often used as a counter-pose to Shoulder Stand.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have serious neck or lower back injuries.

title: Revolved Side Angle (Parivrtta Parsvakonasana)
content: An intense standing twist that builds strength and increases spinal mobility.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have back or hip injuries.

title: Forearm Plank (Phalakasana II)
content: Builds deep core endurance and shoulder stability more intensely than a high plank.
safety_notes: Do not let the lower back sag; keep the tailbone tucked.

title: Garuda Leg Lunge
content: A variation of the lunge incorporating Eagle legs to deepen the stretch in the outer hips.
safety_notes: Ensure the front knee is stable and does not wobble.

title: King Pigeon Pose (Eka Pada Rajakapotasana I)
content: A deep backbend and hip opener that stretches the entire front of the body and strengthens the back.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have acute knee or ankle injuries. Use a strap for the back foot if needed.

title: Side Crow (Parsva Bakasana)
content: A twisting arm balance that strengthens the wrists, arms, and obliques while improving detoxification.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have wrist or lower back injuries.

title: Fire Log Pose (Agnistambhasana)
content: An intense hip opener that targets the outer hips and glutes. It is excellent for increasing rotation in the hip joints.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have knee injuries. Place a blanket between the knees if there is space.

title: Marichi's Pose C (Marichyasana C)
content: A seated twist that stretches the spine and stimulates the digestive organs.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have a spinal disc injury or are pregnant.

title: Heron Pose (Krounchasana)
content: A seated pose that deeply stretches the hamstrings of one leg and the quadriceps of the other.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have serious knee or ankle injuries.

title: Scale Pose (Tolasana)
content: An arm balance performed from a cross-legged position. It strengthens the core, wrists, and arms.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have shoulder or wrist injuries.

title: Compass Pose (Parivrtta Surya Yantrasana)
content: A seated pose that requires high flexibility in the hamstrings and shoulders. It stretches the side body.
safety_notes: Only attempt if hamstrings and shoulders are well-warmed.

title: Humble Warrior (Baddha Virabhadrasana)
content: A standing pose that builds leg strength and opens the shoulders and hips through a forward fold.
safety_notes: Ensure the front knee stays aligned over the ankle to protect the joint.

title: Reclining Hero Pose (Supta Virasana)
content: An intense stretch for the thighs, knees, and ankles. It relieves tired legs and helps with digestion.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have serious back, knee, or ankle injuries.

title: Bird of Paradise (Svarga Dvijasana)
content: A complex standing balance that requires hip mobility and shoulder flexibility while bound.
safety_notes: Warm up the hamstrings and shoulders thoroughly before attempting.

title: Gate Pose Variation (Parighasana II)
content: A deep side-bend that stretches the intercostal muscles and hamstrings while opening the chest.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have recent abdominal surgery.

title: Revolved Half Moon (Parivrtta Ardha Chandrasana)
content: A challenging balance and twist that improves core stability and hip strength.
safety_notes: Use a block under the bottom hand to maintain a straight spine.

title: Peacock Pose (Mayurasana)
content: An arm balance where the body is held horizontal. It strengthens the forearms and detoxifies abdominal organs.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have wrist pain or high blood pressure.

title: Frog Pose (Mandukasana)
content: An intense hip opener that targets the adductors. It helps improve flexibility in the pelvic region.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have acute knee or hip injuries.

title: Splits Pose (Hanumanasana)
content: A deep stretch for the hamstrings and hip flexors. It builds patience and flexibility.
safety_notes: Use blocks under the hands for support to prevent over-stretching.

title: One-Legged King Pigeon II
content: A deep backbend that opens the chest and hip flexors while strengthening the spine.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have lower back pain or hip replacement history.

title: Lotus Pose (Padmasana)
content: The traditional pose for meditation. It calms the mind and opens the hips and ankles.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have knee injuries; try Half-Lotus instead.

title: Feathered Peacock Pose - Prep (Pincha Mayurasana Prep)
content: Forearm stand preparation that builds the necessary shoulder and core strength.
safety_notes: Focus on keeping the elbows shoulder-width apart.

title: Revolved Head-to-Knee Pose (Parivrtta Janu Sirsasana)
content: A seated twist and side stretch that opens the ribs and stretches the hamstrings.
safety_notes: Keep the chest open and avoid collapsing forward toward the floor.

title: Upward Plank Pose (Purvottanasana)
content: Strengthens the triceps, back, and legs while stretching the front of the shoulders and chest.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have carpal tunnel syndrome or neck injuries.

title: One-Legged Bridge Pose (Eka Pada Setu Bandhasana)
content: A variation of Bridge Pose that increases the challenge to the glutes and core.
safety_notes: Keep the hips level to avoid straining the lower back.

title: Noose Pose (Pasasana)
content: A deep squat and twist that stretches the spine and improves digestion.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have knee or lower back issues.

title: Scissor Pose (Variation of Eka Pada Koundinyasana II)
content: An arm balance that stretches the groins while building immense upper body strength.
safety_notes: Only attempt after a thorough hip and hamstring warm-up.

title: Ear-Pressure Pose (Karnapidasana)
content: An inversion that stretches the spine and calms the nervous system by blocking out external noise.
safety_notes: Avoid with neck injuries or during menstruation.

title: Aitken's Pose (Flying Lizard)
content: A challenging arm balance that combines the hip opening of Lizard Pose with the strength of Crow Pose.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have wrist or shoulder issues.

title: Grasshopper Pose (Maksiakasana)
content: A complex twisting arm balance that requires hip rotation and arm strength.
safety_notes: Requires high level of hip mobility; do not force the twist.

title: Revolved Abdomen Pose (Jathara Parivartanasana)
content: A lying twist with straight legs that strengthens the core and detoxifies the body.
safety_notes: Keep the shoulders grounded; avoid lifting them off the mat.

title: Baby Grasshopper Pose
content: A beginner-friendly version of a twisting arm balance that opens the hips and hamstrings.
safety_notes: Focus on the placement of the foot to ensure stability.

title: Eight-Angle Pose (Astavakrasana)
content: A sophisticated twisting arm balance that strengthens the core and arms.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have wrist, elbow, or shoulder injuries.

title: Bound Triangle Pose (Baddha Trikonasana)
content: A variation of Triangle Pose with a bind, deepening the stretch in the chest and shoulders.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have shoulder injuries or rotator cuff issues.

title: Headstand (Sirsasana)
content: Known as the 'King of Poses,' this inversion improves circulation, stimulates the pineal and pituitary glands, and strengthens the core and neck.
safety_notes: High risk for neck injuries. Avoid if you have high blood pressure, glaucoma, or recent neck surgery.

title: Handstand (Adho Mukha Vrksasana)
content: A full inversion that builds incredible shoulder, arm, and wrist strength while improving overall balance and confidence.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have wrist, shoulder, or back injuries, or frequent headaches.

title: Feathered Peacock Pose (Pincha Mayurasana)
content: A forearm balance that requires open shoulders and a strong core. It improves balance and calms the brain.
safety_notes: Do not attempt without sufficient shoulder mobility. Avoid with heart conditions.

title: Scorpion Pose (Vrischikasana)
content: A dramatic inversion where the legs reach over the head toward the face while balancing on the forearms.
safety_notes: Extremely advanced backbend. Avoid if you have hip or back issues or high blood pressure.

title: Firefly Pose (Tittibhasana)
content: An arm balance that requires deep hamstring flexibility and core strength to lift the legs straight out.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have wrist, shoulder, or lower back injuries.

title: One-Legged Arm Balance (Eka Pada Koundinyasana I)
content: A twisted arm balance that challenges the obliques and requires open hamstrings and hip flexors.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have lower back issues or wrist strain.

title: One-Legged Arm Balance II (Eka Pada Koundinyasana II)
content: Focuses on the inner thighs and hamstrings. The legs are split in the air while balancing on the arms.
safety_notes: Ensure shoulders are level to avoid rotator cuff strain.

title: King Pigeon Pose (Full Rajakapotasana)
content: A profound backbend where the back foot is pulled to the head. It stretches the entire front of the body.
safety_notes: Requires extreme spinal and hip flexibility. Use a strap to prevent over-straining.

title: Formidable Pose (Gandha Bherundasana)
content: An intense chin stand and backbend that requires maximum flexibility in the spine and shoulders.
safety_notes: High risk for the neck and throat. Should only be practiced with a teacher.

title: Shoulder-Pressing Pose (Bhujapidasana)
content: An arm balance where the body is supported by the hands while the thighs rest on the upper arms.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have wrist or shoulder injuries.

title: One-Legged Crow Pose (Eka Pada Bakasana)
content: A variation of Crow Pose where one leg is extended straight back into the air.
safety_notes: Requires intense core engagement and wrist strength.

title: Flying Pigeon Pose (Eka Pada Galavasana)
content: An arm balance that requires the hip flexibility of Pigeon Pose and the strength of Crow Pose.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have knee injuries as the foot hooks the arm tightly.

title: Plow Pose with Bind (Baddha Halasana)
content: A variation of Plow Pose where the arms are bound, increasing the stretch in the upper back and neck.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have neck or shoulder issues. Do not turn the head while in the pose.

title: Side Plank with Leg Lift (Vasisthasana B)
content: Side plank while holding the big toe of the top leg and extending it toward the ceiling.
safety_notes: Requires strong hamstrings and exceptional side-body strength.

title: Standing Split (Urdhva Prasarita Eka Padasana)
content: A balance and deep stretch where one leg stays grounded and the other reaches toward the ceiling.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have recent hamstring tears or lower back issues.

title: Full Wheel Pose (Chakrasana)
content: A deep backbend that creates a circle with the body. It strengthens the entire back body.
safety_notes: Avoid with carpal tunnel, heart problems, or chronic back pain.

title: Tortoise Pose (Kurmasana)
content: A seated forward fold where the arms are tucked under the legs. It symbolizes inner withdrawal.
safety_notes: Requires extreme hip and hamstring mobility. Avoid if you have a herniated disc.

title: Peacock Pose in Lotus (Padma Mayurasana)
content: A combination of the Peacock arm balance and the Lotus seated pose.
safety_notes: Highly stressful for the wrists and knees. Use caution.

title: Upward Lotus (Urdhva Padmasana in Sirsasana)
content: Performing the Lotus pose while in a full Headstand.
safety_notes: Requires mastery of both the Headstand and the Lotus pose.

title: One-Armed Handstand (Eka Hasta Adho Mukha Vrksasana)
content: The peak of balancing poses, requiring immense focus, core, and shoulder power.
safety_notes: Extremely high risk of falling. Practicing near a wall is essential.

title: Embryo in Headstand (Pindasana in Sirsasana)
content: A variation where the legs are in lotus and drawn down toward the chest while inverted.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have neck, hip, or knee issues.

title: Knee-to-Ear Headstand
content: A variation of Headstand that requires significant abdominal control and spinal flexibility.
safety_notes: Maintain weight on the forearms, not the neck.

title: Standing Compass Pose
content: A standing version of the seated Compass pose, requiring total body balance and open hips.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have unstable hips or severe hamstring tightness.

title: Full Bow Pose (Poorna Dhanurasana)
content: A deep backbend where the hands reach back to grab the toes with elbows pointing upward.
safety_notes: High intensity for the shoulders and lower back.

title: Yogi Staff Pose (Yoga Dandasana)
content: A seated pose where one foot is placed in the armpit, resembling a staff.
safety_notes: Extremely intense for the hip and knee joints. Risk of meniscus injury if forced.

title: Dragonfly Pose (Maksikanasana)
content: A complex arm balance that involves a deep twist and resting the thigh on the back of the upper arm while the other leg extends horizontally.
safety_notes: Requires high hip mobility and wrist strength. Avoid if you have lower back or shoulder injuries.

title: Two-Legged Crane Pose (Dwi Pada Bakasana)
content: An advanced arm balance where the knees are tucked into the armpits and the arms are fully straightened, lifting the entire body weight.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have carpal tunnel syndrome or shoulder instability.

title: Shoulder-Stand with Lotus (Padma Sarvangasana)
content: A combination of a full shoulder stand and the lotus pose. It stimulates the thyroid and calms the nervous system.
safety_notes: Do not turn your head in this pose. Avoid if you have neck injuries or high blood pressure.

title: One-Legged Wheel Pose (Eka Pada Urdhva Dhanurasana)
content: A variation of the full wheel where one leg is extended straight toward the ceiling, challenging the core and shoulder stability.
safety_notes: Ensure your base foot is stable. Avoid if you have acute back pain or wrist issues.

title: Bound Garland Pose (Baddha Malasana)
content: A deep squat where the arms wrap around the back and legs to create a bind, deepening the stretch in the shoulders and hips.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have chronic knee or ankle issues.

title: Peacock Pose in Lotus (Padma Mayurasana)
content: An arm balance with legs in Lotus pose. It provides a deep detox to the abdominal organs and builds massive forearm strength.
safety_notes: Extremely intense on the wrists and digestive system. Practice on an empty stomach.

title: Handstand with Lotus (Padma Adho Mukha Vrksasana)
content: A full handstand where the legs are folded into the Lotus position while inverted.
safety_notes: Requires mastery of the handstand. Avoid if you have unstable knee ligaments.

title: Wounded Peacock (Eka Hasta Mayurasana)
content: The one-armed version of the peacock pose. It requires near-perfect center of gravity control and wrist strength.
safety_notes: High risk of wrist strain. Only for practitioners with elite upper body strength.

title: Pose Dedicated to Sage Koundinya (Eka Pada Koundinyasana I)
content: A twisted arm balance that strengthens the arms and core while improving spinal flexibility and balance.
safety_notes: Ensure your core is fully engaged to protect the lower back.

title: Side Plank with Lotus (Padma Vasisthasana)
content: A side plank variation where the top leg is in half-lotus, requiring incredible balance and hip flexibility.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have lateral knee pain or shoulder impingement.

title: Supported Headstand II (Sirsasana II)
content: Often called Tripod Headstand, where the weight is distributed between the head and the palms of the hands.
safety_notes: Place more weight on the hands than the head to protect the cervical spine.

title: Flying Crow Pose (Eka Pada Galavasana)
content: A variation of the arm balance where one leg is hooked over the arms and the other is extended straight back.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have knee injuries; the hook requires a deep, safe hip rotation.

title: Firefly Pose Variation (B-Tittibhasana)
content: A standing variation where the feet are behind the head, requiring extreme hamstring and hip flexibility.
safety_notes: High risk of pulling a hamstring if not properly warmed up.

title: Inverted Staff Pose (Dwi Pada Viparita Dandasana)
content: An advanced backbend on the forearms that opens the chest, heart, and shoulders while strengthening the legs.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have high blood pressure or a history of spinal disc herniation.

title: Split Leg Headstand (Eka Pada Sirsasana)
content: A headstand where one leg remains vertical and the other is lowered toward the floor or behind the head.
safety_notes: Requires intense core control to prevent tipping over.

title: Eight-Angle Pose (Astavakrasana)
content: A powerful twisting arm balance that strengthens the wrists and arms and tones the abdominal muscles.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have elbow or shoulder injuries.

title: Bound Half-Moon (Baddha Ardha Chandrasana)
content: A standing balance where the top arm reaches back to grab the top foot, creating a deep chest opening.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have balance issues or knee instability.

title: Pigeon Pose in Handstand
content: Bringing one leg into the pigeon shape while holding a full handstand against a wall or in space.
safety_notes: High risk of falling. Ensure your handstand is stable before trying leg variations.

title: Formidable Face Pose (Ganda Bherundasana)
content: A chin stand with a deep backbend where the feet come over the head to touch the ground in front of the face.
safety_notes: Extreme pressure on the neck and chin. Do not attempt without professional guidance.

title: Full Splits (Hanumanasana)
content: Named after the monkey god, this pose involves one leg extended forward and the other back in a full line.
safety_notes: Go slow; do not force the hips to the floor if you feel sharp pain in the hamstrings.

title: Half-Bound Lotus Standing Fold
content: Standing on one leg with the other in half-lotus while folding forward to touch the floor.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have meniscus issues in the lotus leg.

title: Mountain Pose on Tiptoes with Bind
content: A balance-intensive variation of Tadasana that challenges the central nervous system and ankle strength.
safety_notes: Avoid if you have inner-ear issues or frequent vertigo.

title: One-Legged Inverted Staff Pose
content: A variation of the backbend on the forearms where one leg is lifted vertically into the air.
safety_notes: Requires immense back strength and shoulder flexibility.

title: Embryo Pose (Pindasana)
content: A variation of shoulder stand where the legs are in lotus and the arms wrap around them.
safety_notes: Restricts breathing slightly; stay calm and take shallow, steady breaths.

title: Corpse Pose (Savasana) - Deep Meditation
content: While physically easy, the advanced version involves deep yoga nidra (psychic sleep) and total withdrawal of senses.
safety_notes: If you fall asleep, you may miss the meditative benefits; try to stay conscious.
